newsitem.title: USA: Six-month jail term for U.S. sex-charge sergeant.
newsitem.headline: Six-month jail term for U.S. sex-charge sergeant.

text.p: An army sergeant convicted of sexual misconduct at the Aberdeen Proving Ground was sentenced on Friday to six months in a military jail.

Army Staff Sgt. Vernell Robinson, Jr., a 13-year veteran, hugged his mother and brother after the sentence was announced. He had tearfully apologised to jurors shortly before they began their sentencing deliberations.
"I got the devil in me," Robinson told jurors.

The panel of six men and one woman deliberated 3 hours and 25 minutes before deciding on the sentence, which also includes reduction to the lowest military rank, dishonourable discharge and forfeiture of all pay and benefits.
Robinson, 32, faced a possible jail sentence of 60 years, 6 months. His 6-month term may be served at Quantico, Virginia, or at Fort Knox.

He was convicted after a two-day trial on 19 of the 20 charges he faced. After deliberating five hours on Thursday, jurors found him guilty of violating orders and regulations, sodomy, assault, adultery, obstruction of justice, communicating a threat and soliciting an offence. They acquitted him of interfering with the mail.

Robinson, who served as a drill instructor at the Ordnance Centre and School, is one of four trainers at the Aberdeen Proving Ground charged as a result of an investigation into sexual harassment of female trainees. Eight other soldiers were charged with lesser sexual misconduct in a controversial investigation that was first disclosed in November 1996 and led to an Army-wide probe of sexual harassment.
Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson was sentenced this month to 25 years on convictions of raping six female trainees.
